title: Mrs. Vivien Hidary: Ahare Mot- "Inner Holiness"

chapters.title: Dedications and Yom HaShoah
chapters.about: Memorializing victims of the Holocaust and the concept of Gevurah.

chapters.title: Aaron's Courage in Aharei Mot
chapters.about: Aaron's response to the death of his sons and the choice to continue serving.

chapters.title: Transitioning from Mitzrayim to Eretz Kena'an
chapters.about: The shift from following Moshe and Aaron to personal responsibility.

chapters.title: From Levi to Yehuda
chapters.about: The shift in leadership modality from Moshe to Boaz.

chapters.title: The Symbolism of Barley and Wheat
chapters.about: The spiritual meaning of the Omer offerings and the danger of self-reliance.

chapters.title: Documenting Our Story
chapters.about: The Oneg Shabbat group and the importance of recording history.

summary: Mrs. Hidary explores the themes of Parashat Aharei Mot in the context of Yom HaShoah, focusing on the courage required to rebuild after tragedy. She connects the counting of the Omer to a spiritual progression from the barley offering of Pesach to the wheat offering of Shavuot, representing a journey from dependency to personal responsibility.
questions: How does Aaron's reaction to the loss of his sons relate to the themes of Yom HaShoah?
What is the significance of the transition from barley to wheat during the Omer?
How does the counting of the Omer connect our past to our future?
Why is it important to maintain a connection to Hashem even when we feel secure and successful?
